After heavy rain, water should move toward the roof’s drains and scuppers. When it continues collecting in low areas, that ponding water may point to blocked drainage, an uneven roof surface, or changes within the roofing assembly that deserve a closer look.

Pooling water doesn’t automatically mean a commercial roof needs replacement. It does mean the affected areas should be documented and evaluated before repeated exposure begins affecting seams, flashing, or other vulnerable details.

After the next round of rain, include drainage areas in your property walk-through. What remains on the roof can provide useful information about its current condition.
